peter.name: Peter
peter.role: Apostle of Jesus Christ and fellow elder
peter.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
peter.importance: Peter greets believers living as foreigners in the Dispersion. He tells the elders to shepherd the flock willingly. They must not lord it over those in their care. He calls himself a witness of the sufferings of Christ. He sends greetings from Babylon and from Mark, his son.
peter.connections: He writes to believers in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia. He sends the letter through Silvanus.

jesus.name: Jesus Christ
jesus.role: Christ who suffered, rose, and is at God’s right hand
jesus.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jesus.importance: Peter says God raised Jesus Christ from the dead. Christ suffered for us and left an example. When he was cursed, he did not curse back. He trusted the one who judges righteously. Peter says believers will receive a crown when the chief Shepherd is revealed.
jesus.connections: Peter calls him the chief cornerstone and the chief Shepherd. He is also the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.

word.languageNote: This is the dictionary form of the name “Christ.”

sarah.name: Sarah
sarah.role: Holy woman who called Abraham lord
sarah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
sarah.importance: Peter tells wives to be gentle and quiet. He says holy women of the past did so. He says Sarah obeyed Abraham and called him lord. Wives are her children if they do well. They must not be put in fear by any terror.
sarah.connections: Peter names her obeying her husband Abraham. He calls his readers her children if they do well.

abraham.name: Abraham
abraham.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abraham.importance: Peter names Abraham only as the one Sarah obeyed. He tells no story about him. The next verse tells husbands to honor their wives as joint heirs.
abraham.connections: Peter says Sarah obeyed him and called him lord.

noah.name: Noah
noah.role: Man in whose days the ship was built
noah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
noah.importance: Peter says some spirits in prison were disobedient in the days of Noah. God waited patiently while the ship was built. Eight souls were saved through water. Peter calls this a symbol of baptism.
noah.connections: Peter names his days, when God waited patiently. Eight souls were saved through water.

silas.name: Silvanus
silas.role: Faithful brother who helped write the letter
silas.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
silas.importance: Peter says he wrote this brief letter through Silvanus. The letter says nothing more about what Silvanus did. Peter says the letter shows the true grace of God.
silas.connections: Peter calls him our faithful brother, as he considers him.
